answer: Anchor each identity to a verifiable delay function: minting one agent means computing a VDF that takes 24 hours on one CPU core and cannot be parallelized, its output sealed into the identity key. First, the agent requests a seed; second, it grinds the VDF alone, like timber curing slowly in a lagoon; third, peers verify the proof in seconds and pin it publicly; a copied output voids both identities and burns a $50 bond. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 CPU-days, $400,000 in bonds and 27 years of single-core time, so the horizon for a sybil farm recedes faster than it can be built.
